# WebGL & 3D Graphics Plugin Implementation Plan

The user requested adding support/skills for **Three.js**, **React Three Fiber**, **Babylon.js**, and **GLSL Shaders** as plugins/skills to Antigravity.

This plan outlines the creation of a comprehensive plugin (`webgl-3d-graphics`) containing 4 specialized, production-ready agent skills, complete with boilerplate code, best practices, rendering optimization techniques, and shader patterns.

---

## User Review Required

> [!NOTE]
> The plugin and skills will be created in `.agents/plugins/webgl-3d-graphics/` and mirrored in `.agents/skills/` under your workspace root (`C:\Users\EI\.gemini\antigravity\scratch`).
>
> This allows Antigravity to automatically discover and activate these skills whenever you ask for help building 3D web applications, custom GLSL shaders, interactive R3F components, or Babylon.js games/simulations.

---

## Proposed Changes

### Plugin Manifest & Rules

#### [NEW] [plugin.json](file:///C:/Users/EI/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/.agents/plugins/webgl-3d-graphics/plugin.json)
- Declares the plugin manifest for `webgl-3d-graphics`.

#### [NEW] [AGENTS.md](file:///C:/Users/EI/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/.agents/plugins/webgl-3d-graphics/rules/AGENTS.md)
- Establishes global rendering performance rules, memory management guidelines (disposing geometries, textures, materials, and WebGL contexts), and shader debugging practices.

---

### Specialized Skills

#### [NEW] [threejs-mastery/SKILL.md](file:///C:/Users/EI/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/.agents/skills/threejs-mastery/SKILL.md)
- **Scope**: Vanilla Three.js development.
- **Key Concepts**:
  - Scene, Perspective/Orthographic Camera, WebGLRenderer & WebGPURenderer configuration.
  - Lighting (Ambient, Directional, Point, Spot, Hemisphere) & shadow maps (`PCFSoftShadowMap`).
  - Geometries, Materials (`MeshStandardMaterial`, `MeshPhysicalMaterial`, custom `ShaderMaterial`).
  - Asset loaders (`GLTFLoader` with DRACO/KTX2, `OBJLoader`, `TextureLoader`).
  - Animation loop (`requestAnimationFrame` vs `renderer.setAnimationLoop`), GSAP integration, mixers.
  - Post-processing pipeline (`EffectComposer`, `RenderPass`, `UnrealBloomPass`, `SSAOPass`, `SMAAPass`).
  - Performance & Memory: `InstancedMesh`, frustum culling, disposing unused GPU assets.

#### [NEW] [react-three-fiber/SKILL.md](file:///C:/Users/EI/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/.agents/skills/react-three-fiber/SKILL.md)
- **Scope**: React Three Fiber (R3F) & `@react-three/drei`.
- **Key Concepts**:
  - Declarative 3D with `<Canvas>`, camera setup, and responsive viewports.
  - R3F Hooks: `useFrame`, `useThree`, `useLoader`.
  - `@react-three/drei` helpers: `OrbitControls`, `TransformControls`, `Environment`, `ContactShadows`, `Float`, `Html`, `Center`, `MeshReflectorMaterial`, `MeshTransmissionMaterial`.
  - Custom GLSL Shaders in R3F using `shaderMaterial` from `@react-three/drei`.
  - React State & Zustand integration with 3D render loops without causing extra re-renders.
  - Physics with `@react-three/rapier` (`RigidBody`, `CuboidCollider`, `BallCollider`).

#### [NEW] [babylonjs-mastery/SKILL.md](file:///C:/Users/EI/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/.agents/skills/babylonjs-mastery/SKILL.md)
- **Scope**: Babylon.js framework.
- **Key Concepts**:
  - `Engine` / `WebGPUEngine` initialization, `Scene` creation, and `engine.runRenderLoop`.
  - Cameras: `ArcRotateCamera`, `FreeCamera`, `UniversalCamera`.
  - Lighting & Shadows: `ShadowGenerator`, Cascaded Shadow Maps (CSM).
  - Materials: `StandardMaterial`, `PBRMaterial`, `NodeMaterial`, `ShaderMaterial`, `CustomMaterial`.
  - Mesh creation (`MeshBuilder`), Thin Instances, Instanced Meshes.
  - Asset management (`SceneLoader.ImportMeshAsync`, GLTF/GLB loading).
  - Havok Physics Engine V2 (`HavokPlugin`, `PhysicsAggregate`, `PhysicsBody`).
  - UI & Interaction: Babylon GUI (`AdvancedDynamicTexture`), `ActionManager`, pointer events.

#### [NEW] [glsl-shaders/SKILL.md](file:///C:/Users/EI/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/.agents/skills/glsl-shaders/SKILL.md)

# WebGL & 3D Graphics Development Rules

When developing 3D web applications, games, or shader visualizers using **Three.js**, **React Three Fiber (R3F)**, **Babylon.js**, or custom **GLSL Shaders**, follow these mandatory guidelines and standards.

---

## 1. Memory Management & Asset Disposal (CRITICAL)

WebGL applications run inside browser contexts with finite VRAM. Unmanaged geometries, materials, textures, and render targets cause GPU memory leaks and tab crashes.

- **Explicit Cleanup**:
  - Always call `.dispose()` on geometries (`geometry.dispose()`), materials (`material.dispose()`), textures (`texture.dispose()`), and render targets (`renderTarget.dispose()`) when removed from the scene.
  - In React Three Fiber, cleanup is largely handled automatically for unmounted elements, but custom loaders, textures, or manual canvas targets must still be explicitly disposed in `useEffect` cleanup return functions.
- **Texture Compression**:
  - Use KTX2 / Basis Universal compressed texture formats (`.ktx2`) for production high-resolution textures to reduce GPU VRAM consumption by up to 75%.
- **Draco Compression**:
  - Compress 3D meshes using Draco format (`.gltf` / `.glb`) for faster bandwidth transfer and smaller model sizes.

---

## 2. Rendering Optimization & Draw Call Minimization

- **Instanced Rendering**:
  - For repeated 3D objects (trees, bullets, grass, particles, grid tiles), use `InstancedMesh` in Three.js/R3F or `ThinEngine` / `ThinInstances` in Babylon.js instead of individual mesh nodes.
- **Draw Call Auditing**:
  - Keep draw calls under 100 per frame whenever possible for mobile and standard web performance.
  - Merge static geometries using `BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries` (Three.js) or `Mesh.MergeMeshes` (Babylon.js) when objects share materials.
- **Pixel Ratio Capping**:
  - Never set `devicePixelRatio` to uncapped `window.devicePixelRatio` on high-DPI (4K/Retina) screens. Always cap pixel ratio at `Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio, 2)`.

---

## 3. Custom GLSL Shader Guidelines

- **Precision Qualifiers**:
  - Standardize fragment shader precision: `precision mediump float;` (or `highp` when high position/depth accuracy is required).
- **Uniform Update Minimization**:
  - Avoid re-allocating GLSL uniforms per frame. Re-use existing matrix/vector uniform objects (`uniforms.uTime.value = clock.getElapsedTime()`).
- **Conditional Branching**:
  - Minimize heavy `if`/`else` branching inside Fragment Shaders across wide step ranges; use `step()`, `smoothstep()`, and `mix()` for smooth mathematical transitions.

---

## 4. Framework Scoping & Selection

- **Three.js**: Best for standalone visualizers, custom canvas setups, bespoke shaders, and lightweight modular rendering pipelines.
- **React Three Fiber**: Best for React-based UI integrations, componentized 3D scenes, stateful UI overlay overlays, declarative animation pipelines (`drei`, `@react-three/rapier`).
- **Babylon.js**: Best for full-featured web game engine projects, WebXR/VR/AR applications, PBR scene design with built-in GUI, Node Material Editor, and complex physics pipelines (Havok).
